description: Advanced JavaScript runtime semantics, prototypes, lexical environments, deep cloning, and functional composition archetypes.

archetypes.name: Abortable Async Work & Cancellation Cleanup
archetypes.coreConcept: Cancellation is a cooperative signal: an operation observes AbortSignal, stops at safe boundaries, releases resources, and settles according to one documented cancellation contract.
mentalModel: 1. The caller owns an AbortController and communicates cancellation through its signal.
2. The operation checks the signal before starting and at asynchronous boundaries.
3. The operation settles once and completes cleanup without hiding an earlier result.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A cancellation request prevents further work after the next defined cancellation boundary and never leaves listeners or resources attached.

cognitiveTraps.name: Ignoring a Signal That Was Already Aborted
cognitiveTraps.description: Registering only a future abort listener misses cancellation that occurred before the operation began.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Abort the controller before calling the operation, then verify no work starts and the documented cancellation result is returned.

cognitiveTraps.name: Leaving Abort Listeners Attached
cognitiveTraps.description: An operation that finishes normally but never removes its abort listener retains callbacks and may react to a later cancellation.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Complete many operations with one long-lived signal and verify each operation releases its listener after settlement.

cognitiveTraps.name: Late Cancellation Replaces a Settled Result
cognitiveTraps.description: A cancellation event arriving after completion can incorrectly reject or overwrite an already settled operation.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Resolve the operation, then abort its controller and verify the original result remains stable.

realWorldDomains.description: Stopping a large report export when a user navigates away while preserving cleanup and a stable completion contract.
Cancelling queued and in-flight upload work without leaving request listeners or progress state behind.

qualityChecks.check: The operation has one settlement path, and abort events after settlement cannot replace the settled value or error.
qualityChecks.why: Late cancellation must not make callers observe a different outcome from the operation that already completed.

qualityChecks.check: Abort listeners and other operation-owned resources are released on every settlement path.
qualityChecks.why: Unreleased listeners retain closures and allow completed work to react to unrelated later cancellation.

archetypes.name: Lexical Scope Boundary & Variable Shadowing Guard
archetypes.coreConcept: Enforcing block scoping and preventing variable leakage across execution contexts, ensuring outer variables remain accessible without accidental variable shadowing.
mentalModel: 1. Isolate variable bindings inside explicit block and function scopes.
2. Prevent reassignment of outer lexical identifiers.
3. Guarantee clean execution environment without polluting global scope.
archetypes.governingInvariant: innerBindings shadow within block without mutating outer scope bindings

cognitiveTraps.name: Var Declaration Scope Leak
cognitiveTraps.description: Using var instead of let/const causes variable hoisting to function scope, leaking loop variables.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Loop with var i; check outer scope or timeout callback; all closures see terminal i.

realWorldDomains.description: Isolating plugin options from modifying host runtime configuration.

qualityChecks.check: Loop and callback variables are declared with block-scoped `const`/`let` inside each iteration, never hoisted with `var` or shared outside the loop.
qualityChecks.why: Hoisted or shared loop bindings cause closures created inside the loop to read the final mutated value.

qualityChecks.check: Inner helper functions or blocks do not reassign outer configuration bindings passed into the sandbox.
qualityChecks.why: Mutating outer lexical bindings leaks state across independent calls or plugins.

archetypes.name: Prototype Inheritance & Explicit This Binding Invoker
archetypes.coreConcept: Managing dynamic this context binding across detached callbacks and delegating method resolution through the prototype chain.
mentalModel: 1. Explicitly bind context receiver to handlers using Function.prototype.bind or arrow wrappers.
2. Maintain prototype delegation links via Object.create or ES6 classes.
3. Prevent losing execution context when passing methods as event or timer callbacks.
archetypes.governingInvariant: detachedMethod() executes with bound target receiver as this

cognitiveTraps.name: Detached Method Context Loss
cognitiveTraps.description: Passing object.method as a bare callback strips this binding, resulting in undefined or global this.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const cb = obj.method; cb(); throws TypeError cannot read property of undefined.

realWorldDomains.description: Binding subscriber service instances to pub/sub event handlers safely.

qualityChecks.check: Callbacks or detached methods preserve their intended receiver context rather than relying on ambient or unbound `this`.
qualityChecks.why: Passing a bare method reference detaches its `this` receiver and fails or reads `undefined` at call time.
accepted: class arrow field when per-instance binding is needed

qualityChecks.check: Instance methods shared across objects are defined on the class or prototype rather than recreated per instance unless closure privacy requires it.
qualityChecks.why: Attaching identical method closures to every instance breaks prototype delegation and wastes memory.

archetypes.name: Object-to-Primitive Coercion & ValueOf Protocol
archetypes.coreConcept: Diagnosing and remediating defects in arithmetic and string coercion routines implementing Symbol.toPrimitive, valueOf, and toString protocols.
mentalModel: 1. Trace object-to-primitive conversion steps: preferredType hint ('number', 'string', 'default').
2. Validate that valueOf and toString return valid primitive values.
3. Ensure mathematical operations receive numeric primitives rather than string concatenations.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Symbol.toPrimitive(hint) returns primitive adhering to operand expectations

cognitiveTraps.name: String Concatenation in Numeric Arithmetic
cognitiveTraps.description: Returning string from valueOf causes '+' operator to perform string concatenation instead of addition.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Passing object with valueOf() => '10'; obj + 5 yields '105' instead of 15.

cognitiveTraps.name: Non-Primitive Return from Symbol.toPrimitive
cognitiveTraps.description: Returning an object or ignoring the 'string' hint in Symbol.toPrimitive throws TypeError or produces '[object Object]'.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Coerce object in template literal `${obj}`; Symbol.toPrimitive returns {} and throws TypeError.

realWorldDomains.description: Fixing financial currency value objects to perform accurate arithmetic comparisons.

qualityChecks.check: Custom coercion hooks (`Symbol.toPrimitive`, `valueOf`, `toString`) return true primitives matching the requested conversion hint and never return objects.
qualityChecks.why: Returning a non-primitive or wrong primitive type breaks both numeric arithmetic and string interpolation.

qualityChecks.check: Invalid or non-representable inputs in value-object constructors or converters fail with a descriptive domain error rather than silently producing `NaN`.
qualityChecks.why: Silent `NaN` propagation corrupts downstream financial or unit calculations without a clear cause.

archetypes.name: Deep Object Cloner with Circular Reference Handling
archetypes.coreConcept: Recursively duplicating nested objects, arrays, and primitive fields while tracking visited object references via a Map/WeakMap to prevent infinite recursion on circular graphs.
mentalModel: 1. Base case: Return primitive values and functions as-is.
2. Check reference tracker: If object was already cloned, return existing clone reference.
3. Initialize new container (Array or Object) and register in reference map before recursively copying properties.
archetypes.governingInvariant: clone !== original; clone.circularRef === clone; deep mutations do not affect original

cognitiveTraps.name: Call Stack Overflow on Self-Referential Graph
cognitiveTraps.description: Naive JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(x)) or un-memoized recursion crashes with RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const a = {}; a.self = a; deepClone(a); crashes without reference tracking.

cognitiveTraps.name: Registering Clone After Recursing Into Children
cognitiveTraps.description: Storing the new clone in the visited map after cloning child properties still overflows on self-referential cycles.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const a = {}; a.self = a; deepClone(a) recurses infinitely before seen.set(a, copy) is reached.

cognitiveTraps.name: Cloning Arrays as Plain Objects
cognitiveTraps.description: Cloning an Array into '{}' strips Array.isArray identity, prototype methods, and length semantics.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: deepClone([1, 2]) returns { '0': 1, '1': 2 } instead of [1, 2].

realWorldDomains.description: Cloning state trees for time-travel debugging and snapshot isolation.

qualityChecks.check: Object graph traversal records visited references before descending into child properties so cyclic graphs terminate and preserve shared or self-referential identity.
qualityChecks.why: Traversing without pre-registered reference tracking crashes on cycles or duplicates shared subgraphs.

qualityChecks.check: Container allocation preserves runtime collection kind (arrays remain arrays, plain objects remain plain objects) rather than flattening via lossy serialization.
qualityChecks.why: Lossy serialization or `{}`-only cloning drops array semantics, `undefined` fields, and special values.

archetypes.name: Asynchronous Function Composition & Middleware Pipeline
archetypes.coreConcept: Constructing an onion-style asynchronous pipeline (similar to Koa/Express) that chains async middleware functions sequentially with next() downstream dispatch and upstream return propagation.
mentalModel: 1. Enforce that next() cannot be invoked multiple times in a single middleware frame.
2. Cascade execution downstream by awaiting the returned promise of next().
3. Catch downstream exceptions and allow upstream middleware to handle or rethrow them.
archetypes.governingInvariant: dispatch(i) executes middleware[i](context, next); multiple next() calls throw 'next() called multiple times'

cognitiveTraps.name: Multiple Next Invocation Defect
cognitiveTraps.description: Calling next() twice in one middleware branches execution and corrupts pipeline flow.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Middleware calls await next(); await next(); downstream executes duplicate operations.

cognitiveTraps.name: Non-Promise Return Breaking Upstream Await
cognitiveTraps.description: Returning undefined or a synchronous value from dispatch() breaks upstream await next() ordering and error propagation.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Synchronous middleware throws; upstream try { await next(); } catch misses or out-of-order post-next runs.

cognitiveTraps.name: Missing Terminal Dispatch Base Case
cognitiveTraps.description: Failing to resolve cleanly when dispatch index reaches middlewares.length causes TypeError on undefined invocation.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Call composed pipeline with last middleware calling await next(); throws TypeError: fn is not a function.

realWorldDomains.description: Asynchronous HTTP request processing pipeline handling auth, rate-limiting, and logging.

qualityChecks.check: Every dispatch step returns or awaits a promise chain so upstream `try/catch` and post-`next()` hooks run in strict onion order.
qualityChecks.why: Fire-and-forget or non-promise dispatch steps break upstream error catching and post-`next()` ordering.

qualityChecks.check: Dispatch cursor state is scoped per pipeline invocation rather than shared across requests at module or composer scope.
qualityChecks.why: Sharing the dispatch index across concurrent invocations corrupts middleware ordering under load.

archetypes.name: Creation Phase Hoisting & Temporal Dead Zone Trace
archetypes.coreConcept: Tracing how the JavaScript engine allocates bindings during the Creation Phase before executing statements, distinguishing initialized var/function declarations from uninitialized let/const bindings in the Temporal Dead Zone.
mentalModel: 1. Creation Phase registers all declarations in the current LexicalEnvironment before line 1 runs.
2. var bindings initialize to undefined; function declarations initialize to their function object; let/const remain uninitialized (TDZ).
3. Reading or writing a let/const binding before its initializer executes throws ReferenceError.
archetypes.governingInvariant: let/const bindings exist in scope from block entry but throw ReferenceError until their initializer line executes

cognitiveTraps.name: Temporal Dead Zone ReferenceError
cognitiveTraps.description: Assuming an inner block let/const falls back to an outer variable of the same name before its declaration line, instead of throwing ReferenceError.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const rate = 1; { console.log(rate); const rate = 2; } throws ReferenceError instead of logging 1.

cognitiveTraps.name: Function Expression Hoisting Confusion
cognitiveTraps.description: Treating a const/var function expression like a hoisted function declaration and invoking it before assignment.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: runTask(); const runTask = () => 1; throws ReferenceError (or TypeError with var).

realWorldDomains.description: Tracing module startup order and configuration initialization guards.

qualityChecks.check: Bindings declared with `const` or `let` are initialized before any code path in the same scope can read them, avoiding TDZ `ReferenceError` traps.
qualityChecks.why: Inner `let`/`const` declarations shadow outer bindings for the entire block and throw `ReferenceError` if accessed before their initializer.

qualityChecks.check: Helper functions and constants are declared above their first call site so execution order matches reading order without relying on hoisting.
qualityChecks.why: Relying on function hoisting or `var` initialization hides temporal dependencies and breaks when converted to `const` arrow functions.

archetypes.name: Lexical Scope Chain & Shadowing Resolution
archetypes.coreConcept: Diagnosing and fixing scope-chain bugs where nested functions or blocks resolve free variables from their static definition environment rather than their dynamic call site, or accidentally shadow outer parameters.
mentalModel: 1. A function's [[Environment]] is captured at definition time (lexical/static scope), never at call time.
2. Identifier lookup walks outward through lexical parent environments until the first matching binding is found.
3. Accidental shadowing in an inner block hides the outer binding without modifying it.
archetypes.governingInvariant: freeVariable lookup follows static definition-site [[Environment]] chain, independent of call stack

cognitiveTraps.name: Dynamic vs. Lexical Scope Confusion
cognitiveTraps.description: Assuming a function called inside another function reads the caller's local variable instead of its own definition-site outer scope.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const mode = 'prod'; function readMode() { return mode; } function test() { const mode = 'dev'; return readMode(); } returns 'prod', not 'dev'.

cognitiveTraps.name: Accidental Inner Shadowing Masking Outer State
cognitiveTraps.description: Redeclaring a parameter or outer variable inside an inner block shadows the outer binding so updates only affect the inner variable.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: let total = 10; if (flag) { let total = 0; total += 5; } // outer total remains 10.

realWorldDomains.description: Resolving fallback tenant settings across nested scope boundaries without shadowing.

qualityChecks.check: Inner scopes do not redeclare identifier names that already exist in an enclosing scope (`no-shadow`).
qualityChecks.why: Shadowing an outer parameter or variable makes it unclear which binding is read or updated and silently drops outer updates.

qualityChecks.check: Functions that depend on varying runtime context accept it as an explicit parameter rather than relying on ambiguous outer mutable bindings.
qualityChecks.why: Implicitly reading mutable outer variables makes behaviour depend on definition-site state that callers cannot easily see.

archetypes.name: Stateful Closure Factory & Private Encapsulation
archetypes.coreConcept: Creating stateful function or API factories where each invocation allocates a fresh Lexical Environment that encapsulates private state behind controlled methods.
mentalModel: 1. Each call to the outer factory creates a brand-new Lexical Environment for its parameters and local variables.
2. Returned inner functions retain a live [[Environment]] reference to that specific invocation's bindings.
3. Callers interact only through returned methods, preventing direct external mutation of internal state.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Each factory call allocates an isolated Lexical Environment; returned methods never expose raw internal mutable containers

cognitiveTraps.name: Shared Outer State Across Factory Instances
cognitiveTraps.description: Declaring state outside the factory function causes all created instances to share and overwrite the same binding.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: let count = 0; function makeCounter() { return () => ++count; } — two counters increment the same total.

cognitiveTraps.name: Leaking Internal Mutable Container Reference
cognitiveTraps.description: Returning an internal array or object directly from a closure getter lets callers mutate private state externally.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: getItems() { return items; } allows caller.getItems().push('tampered') to bypass validation.

cognitiveTraps.name: Falsy Initial Value Overwritten by Logical OR
cognitiveTraps.description: Using `initial || fallback` inside a factory replaces valid `0`, `false`, or `''` initial values with the fallback.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const start = initial || 10; when initial is 0, start becomes 10 instead of 0.

realWorldDomains.description: Encapsulating per-client request quota and refill state inside a closure.
Memoizing or deduplicating one-time payment/webhook executions per key.

qualityChecks.check: Mutable state for a stateful factory is declared inside the factory body so every factory invocation owns independent state.
qualityChecks.why: Module-level or outer-scope mutable state leaks across independent instances and breaks isolation.

qualityChecks.check: Closure getters or snapshot methods return shallow/defensive copies of internal mutable arrays or objects rather than direct references.
qualityChecks.why: Returning a direct reference allows callers to mutate private closure state outside the factory's invariants.

archetypes.name: Stale Closure & Loop Callback Binding Repair
archetypes.coreConcept: Diagnosing and fixing stale closure bugs where callbacks either capture a shared mutable loop binding or freeze an outdated primitive value instead of reading current state.
mentalModel: 1. Distinguish capturing a live binding (reads latest value on call) from copying a primitive into a parameter or local variable at creation time.
2. In loops, `let` creates a fresh per-iteration binding for each callback, whereas `var` or an outer `let` shares one binding.
3. When a callback needs the latest config/state after updates, read from the live binding or a getter rather than a destructured stale snapshot.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Callbacks observe the intended per-iteration or live state binding without reading stale snapshots or shared loop counters

cognitiveTraps.name: Stale Primitive Snapshot Captured at Registration
cognitiveTraps.description: Copying a primitive property into a local variable before registering a callback causes the callback to see the old value after updates.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const limit = config.limit; register(() => limit); — updating config.limit later leaves the callback returning the old limit.

cognitiveTraps.name: Shared Loop Binding Captured Across Callbacks
cognitiveTraps.description: Declaring the loop counter outside the loop or with `var` causes all created callbacks to read the terminal loop value.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) handlers.push(() => i); — every handler returns 3.

realWorldDomains.description: Scheduling per-route retry handlers that must read live circuit-breaker thresholds or per-route indices.
Registering per-topic event handlers in a loop without cross-topic index collisions.

qualityChecks.check: Callbacks created inside loops bind a fresh block-scoped `const`/`let` per iteration rather than sharing a `var` or outer loop variable.
qualityChecks.why: A shared loop binding mutates on every iteration so deferred callbacks all observe the final value.

qualityChecks.check: Deferred callbacks that must reflect updated state read from a live object/binding rather than caching a stale primitive snapshot at creation time.
qualityChecks.why: Caching a primitive value before registration disconnects the callback from subsequent state updates.

archetypes.name: Live Closure Binding & Environment Tracing
archetypes.coreConcept: Tracing exact outputs of nested closures by tracking which Lexical Environment each function captures and whether sibling closures share one binding or own separate environments.
mentalModel: 1. Two closures returned from the same factory call share that call's Lexical Environment.
2. Two closures returned from different factory calls point to separate Lexical Environments.
3. Updating an outer `let` binding inside one sibling closure is immediately visible to the other sibling.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Closures created in the same outer call share live bindings; closures from separate outer calls have disjoint bindings

cognitiveTraps.name: Confusing Live Binding with Creation-Time Value
cognitiveTraps.description: Assuming a closure freezes the value of an outer variable when the function is defined rather than reading its current value when invoked.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: let tax = 5; const fn = () => tax; tax = 8; fn() returns 8, not 5.

cognitiveTraps.name: Confusing Shared Sibling Scope with Separate Factory Calls
cognitiveTraps.description: Misidentifying whether two closures share one outer environment (same call) or have independent environments (separate calls).
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const a = makePair(); const b = makePair(); a.inc(); b.read() returns 0, not 1.

realWorldDomains.description: Tracing live toggle overrides across shared reader/writer closures in a config module.

qualityChecks.check: Closures that mutate shared outer state expose explicit, named operations rather than implicit side effects inside readers.
qualityChecks.why: Hidden mutations inside getter-like closures make execution traces unpredictable.

qualityChecks.check: Separate logical instances are created through separate factory calls rather than sharing a single outer mutable binding.
qualityChecks.why: Sharing an outer binding across unrelated instances couples their state transitions unexpectedly.

archetypes.name: Call-Site This Binding & Arrow Lexical This Trace
archetypes.coreConcept: Predicting the runtime value of this across implicit method calls, detached strict-mode calls, explicit call/apply/bind overrides, new construction, and arrow functions that inherit lexical this from their enclosing scope.
mentalModel: 1. Regular functions determine this dynamically at the call site: new > explicit (call/apply/bind) > implicit (obj.fn) > default (undefined in strict mode).
2. Arrow functions have no own this; they capture this lexically from the enclosing scope at definition time.
3. Object literals do not create a lexical this scope, so an arrow property on an object literal captures the surrounding scope's this.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Regular function this follows call-site precedence (new > explicit > implicit > default); arrow this follows enclosing lexical scope

cognitiveTraps.name: Arrow Method on Object Literal Capturing Outer This
cognitiveTraps.description: Assuming an arrow function defined directly on an object literal binds this to that object instead of the enclosing scope.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const svc = { rate: 2, calc: () => this.rate }; svc.calc() reads outer this.rate (undefined), not 2.

cognitiveTraps.name: Detached Method Falling Back to Strict Undefined
cognitiveTraps.description: Assuming a method reference extracted into a local variable remembers its original object when invoked bare.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: 'use strict'; const fn = obj.read; fn(); throws TypeError because this is undefined.

realWorldDomains.description: Tracing this resolution across service method calls, detached callbacks, and arrow handlers.

qualityChecks.check: Trace helpers and adapters pass explicit receiver objects or bound functions rather than relying on ambient global this.
qualityChecks.why: Implicit default binding resolves to undefined in strict mode and globalThis in sloppy mode, causing environment-dependent bugs.

qualityChecks.check: Arrow functions are used only where lexical this is intended, never as object-literal or prototype methods that expect a dynamic receiver.
qualityChecks.why: An arrow function on an object literal or prototype cannot receive the instance as this.

archetypes.name: Callback & Event Handler This Binding Repair
archetypes.coreConcept: Diagnosing and repairing lost-receiver bugs where methods are passed as callbacks to higher-order array methods, timers, or event dispatchers, or where nested regular functions shadow outer this.
mentalModel: 1. Passing obj.method as a bare argument detaches the call site from obj.
2. A nested regular function inside a method gets its own dynamic this (undefined in strict mode), shadowing the outer method's this.
3. Preserve the intended receiver with an arrow callback, Function.prototype.bind, or explicit thisArg.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Callbacks invoked by external dispatchers or array iterators execute with the service instance as this

cognitiveTraps.name: Nested Regular Function Shadowing Outer This
cognitiveTraps.description: Using a regular function expression inside Array.prototype.map/filter/forEach shadows the enclosing method's this with undefined.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: items.map(function (x) { return this.prefix + x; }) throws TypeError reading prefix of undefined.

cognitiveTraps.name: Attempting to Rebind an Arrow Function with Call or Bind
cognitiveTraps.description: Calling .call(ctx) or .bind(ctx) on an arrow function silently ignores ctx because arrow functions have lexical this.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const fn = () => this.id; fn.call({ id: 42 }) still reads the outer lexical this, not 42.

realWorldDomains.description: Fixing lost this inside array map callbacks on an invoice formatting service.
Fixing arrow-vs-regular callback binding when invoking handler plugins with explicit receiver context.

qualityChecks.check: Callbacks passed to iterators, timers, or dispatchers preserve the intended receiver via .bind(), arrow wrappers, or explicit thisArg.
qualityChecks.why: Detached method references or nested regular functions lose their receiver and throw TypeError or read undefined.

qualityChecks.check: Methods avoid legacy `const self = this` / `const that = this` aliasing when arrow callbacks or `.bind()` express the lexical receiver directly.
qualityChecks.why: Manual `self`/`that` aliasing adds boilerplate and obscures lexical binding intent.

archetypes.name: Prototype Chain Property Lookup & Shadowing Trace
archetypes.coreConcept: Tracing property lookup along the [[Prototype]] chain, distinguishing own properties from inherited properties, and predicting how property assignment shadows rather than mutates prototype properties.
mentalModel: 1. Reading obj.prop walks obj -> Object.getPrototypeOf(obj) -> ... -> null until the first matching key is found.
2. Assigning obj.prop = val creates or updates an own property on obj, shadowing any prototype property without mutating the prototype.
3. Object.hasOwn(obj, key) checks only own properties, whereas `key in obj` traverses the entire [[Prototype]] chain.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Property reads walk the [[Prototype]] chain; direct assignment writes an own property on the receiver

cognitiveTraps.name: Confusing Constructor.prototype with Object.getPrototypeOf(Constructor)
cognitiveTraps.description: Assuming Fn.prototype is Fn's own [[Prototype]], when Fn.prototype is the prototype assigned to instances created with `new Fn()` while Object.getPrototypeOf(Fn) is Function.prototype.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Object.getPrototypeOf(Widget) === Widget.prototype // false; Object.getPrototypeOf(new Widget()) === Widget.prototype // true.

cognitiveTraps.name: Using `in` Operator for Own-Property Checks
cognitiveTraps.description: Using `key in obj` to test membership on a plain object returns true for inherited Object.prototype keys like `toString` or `constructor`.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: 'toString' in {} // true, causing dictionary lookups to collide with Object.prototype methods.

cognitiveTraps.name: Confusing Property Shadowing with Prototype Mutation
cognitiveTraps.description: Assuming `instance.limit = 5` mutates `proto.limit` for all sibling instances when `limit` is a primitive on the prototype.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const a = Object.create(proto); a.limit = 5; // proto.limit and sibling b.limit remain unchanged.

realWorldDomains.description: Tracing environment-to-default configuration lookup and per-tenant overrides via prototype delegation.

qualityChecks.check: Own-property existence checks on plain objects use `Object.hasOwn(obj, key)` (or `Object.create(null)` dictionaries) rather than `key in obj`.
qualityChecks.why: `key in obj` walks the prototype chain and matches inherited `Object.prototype` keys such as `toString` or `constructor`.

qualityChecks.check: Prototype inspection and delegation use `Object.getPrototypeOf` / `Object.create` rather than deprecated `__proto__` accessors.
qualityChecks.why: `__proto__` is a legacy Annex B accessor absent on `Object.create(null)` objects and slower than standard `Object` helpers.

archetypes.name: Shared Mutable Prototype State Repair
archetypes.coreConcept: Diagnosing and fixing cross-instance state pollution caused by storing mutable arrays, objects, Maps, or Sets on a prototype or mutating nested inherited objects in place.
mentalModel: 1. Primitive properties on a prototype are shadowed on write, but mutating methods like `.push()` or `.set()` on an inherited object read the prototype reference and mutate it in place.
2. All mutable per-instance containers must be allocated inside the constructor or factory for each instance.
3. Overriding a nested inherited config object requires creating a fresh copy on the instance instead of mutating the prototype's nested property.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Mutating one instance's state never mutates prototype-shared containers or sibling instances

cognitiveTraps.name: Mutable Container Placed on Prototype
cognitiveTraps.description: Defining `Base.prototype.items = []` or sharing a mutable object in `Object.create(template)` causes `.push()` on one instance to appear in all instances.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function Bag() {} Bag.prototype.items = []; const a = new Bag(); const b = new Bag(); a.items.push('x'); b.items // ['x'].

cognitiveTraps.name: In-Place Mutation of Nested Inherited Object
cognitiveTraps.description: Modifying a property inside an inherited object (`instance.settings.retries = 5`) mutates the shared prototype's `settings` object instead of shadowing `settings` on `instance`.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const a = Object.create({ settings: { retries: 1 } }); a.settings.retries = 5; // affects prototype and all siblings.

realWorldDomains.description: Isolating per-session event logs and tag lists across prototype-linked session objects.

qualityChecks.check: Mutable per-instance state (arrays, objects, maps, sets) is initialized on each instance in the constructor or factory rather than shared on a prototype.
qualityChecks.why: Mutating an array or object inherited from a prototype leaks changes across every instance sharing that prototype.

qualityChecks.check: When an instance customizes an inherited nested configuration object, it clones or replaces the nested object on the instance before mutating.
qualityChecks.why: Writing `this.config.key = val` when `this.config` lives on the prototype mutates the prototype's nested object for all siblings.

archetypes.name: Prototype Delegation Hierarchy & Null-Prototype Dictionary
archetypes.coreConcept: Implementing clean prototype delegation chains via ES6 `class extends` or `Object.create`, placing shared methods on the prototype, walking chains safely with `Object.getPrototypeOf`, and using `Object.create(null)` for collision-free dictionaries.
mentalModel: 1. `class Sub extends Base` links `Sub.prototype.[[Prototype]] === Base.prototype` and requires `super(...)` before accessing `this`.
2. Walking a prototype chain terminates when `Object.getPrototypeOf(cursor) === null`.
3. `Object.create(null)` creates a dictionary with no `Object.prototype`, so `Object.hasOwn(dict, key)` must be used instead of `dict.hasOwnProperty(key)`.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Shared methods live on the prototype, per-instance state lives on the instance, and chain traversal stops at null

cognitiveTraps.name: Accessing `this` Before `super()` or Omitting `super()`
cognitiveTraps.description: In a subclass constructor, `this` is uninitialized until `super()` executes; accessing `this` first throws ReferenceError.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: class Sub extends Base { constructor(x) { this.x = x; super(); } } throws ReferenceError.

cognitiveTraps.name: Calling Object.prototype Methods on Null-Prototype Object
cognitiveTraps.description: Calling `dict.hasOwnProperty(k)` or `dict.toString()` on `Object.create(null)` throws TypeError because it has no Object.prototype.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const d = Object.create(null); d.hasOwnProperty('a') throws TypeError: d.hasOwnProperty is not a function.

cognitiveTraps.name: Overwriting Fn.prototype Without Preserving Chain
cognitiveTraps.description: Replacing `Fn.prototype = { ... }` discards the default `constructor` link and any prior inheritance link.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Sub.prototype = { run() {} }; new Sub() instanceof Base // false.

realWorldDomains.description: Building a two-level adapter hierarchy and prototype-safe key-value registry.

qualityChecks.check: Shared instance methods are defined on the class or prototype rather than recreated as per-instance closures in the constructor.
qualityChecks.why: Recreating identical methods per instance wastes memory and bypasses prototype delegation.

qualityChecks.check: Null-prototype dictionaries (`Object.create(null)`) are queried with `Object.hasOwn(dict, key)` rather than instance methods like `dict.hasOwnProperty(key)`.
qualityChecks.why: Objects created with `Object.create(null)` have no `Object.prototype` and throw `TypeError` when `hasOwnProperty` is called as a method.

archetypes.name: ESM & CJS Export Structure and Import Resolution
archetypes.coreConcept: Structuring ES Module and CommonJS exports cleanly with explicit named exports, avoiding default-vs-named import mismatches and barrel re-export collisions.
mentalModel: 1. Named exports (`export { fn }`) bind exact identifiers and require matching `{ fn }` destructured imports in ESM.
2. Default exports (`export default ...`) bind a single unnamed value per module and are imported without braces.
3. Barrel `index` files must alias colliding names (`export { parse as parseCsv } from './csv.js'`) to keep the public API unambiguous.
archetypes.governingInvariant: every imported symbol resolves to its intended exported binding without name collisions or undefined destructuring

cognitiveTraps.name: Default vs. Named Export Mismatch
cognitiveTraps.description: Importing a default export using `{ name }` or importing a named export without braces produces `undefined` or a `SyntaxError`.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Module exports `export default function parse() {}`; consumer writes `import { parse } from './parser.js'` -> SyntaxError.

cognitiveTraps.name: Barrel Re-Export Name Collision
cognitiveTraps.description: Using `export *` from two submodules that export the same identifier causes an ambiguous export error or silent shadowing.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: index.js does `export * from './v1.js'; export * from './v2.js';` where both export `normalize` -> SyntaxError / ambiguity.

realWorldDomains.description: Structuring a modular feature-flag SDK with clean named exports and conflict-free barrel re-exports.

qualityChecks.check: Module boundaries expose explicit named exports rather than mutating globals or mixing ambiguous default and named exports for the same symbol.
qualityChecks.why: Explicit named exports enable static analysis, reliable refactoring, and prevent default-vs-named import mismatches.

qualityChecks.check: Importing a module does not trigger hidden global mutations or side-effectful initialization at top-level evaluation time.
qualityChecks.why: Import-time side effects make module load order fragile and break deterministic testing.

archetypes.name: Circular Import & Evaluation Order Resolution
archetypes.coreConcept: Diagnosing and resolving circular import bugs where top-level module evaluation reads an uninitialized ESM binding (TDZ) or an incomplete CommonJS `exports` object.
mentalModel: 1. In ESM, modules are linked before evaluation; reading an uninitialized `const`/`let` binding from a cyclic dependency at top level throws `ReferenceError`.
2. In CJS, a cyclic `require()` returns the partially populated `exports` object as it exists at that moment; reassigning `module.exports` later leaves the cycle with stale `{}`.
3. Break cycles by extracting shared constants/helpers into a third leaf module, or deferring cross-module reads into function bodies.
archetypes.governingInvariant: module graph evaluation completes without reading uninitialized cyclic bindings or stale partial exports

cognitiveTraps.name: Top-Level Read of Uninitialized Cyclic Binding
cognitiveTraps.description: Calling or reading a cyclic import during top-level module execution hits the Temporal Dead Zone in ESM or `undefined` in CJS.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: a.js imports `config` from b.js and reads `config.port` at top level while b.js imports `init` from a.js -> ReferenceError.

cognitiveTraps.name: CommonJS module.exports Reassignment in Cycle
cognitiveTraps.description: Reassigning `module.exports = ...` after a cyclic `require()` leaves the requiring module holding the original empty `exports` object.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: a.js requires b.js which requires a.js; a.js later sets `module.exports = { run }` -> b.js sees `{}`.

realWorldDomains.description: Resolving a circular import between token verifier and session store modules in an auth service.

qualityChecks.check: Shared constants, types, or helpers needed by mutually referencing modules are extracted into an acyclic leaf module or accessed lazily inside functions rather than at top level.
qualityChecks.why: Top-level reads across a cycle depend on fragile import order and fail with TDZ ReferenceError or partial exports.

qualityChecks.check: All imported module bindings are actively used without dead imports or shadowed local declarations.
qualityChecks.why: Unused imports create false dependency edges in the module graph and can trigger unnecessary cycles.

archetypes.name: ESM Live Bindings vs. CJS Value Copies & Singleton Cache
archetypes.coreConcept: Tracing how ESM exports expose live read-only views into the exporting module's scope while CJS `require()` copies primitive values at import time, and how both cache module singletons per specifier.
mentalModel: 1. Every module specifier is evaluated once and cached in the module map; subsequent imports return the same cached instance.
2. ESM `import { count }` is a live read-only binding: updates inside the exporting module are visible to all importers, but importers cannot reassign `count`.
3. CJS `const { count } = require('./mod')` copies the primitive value at require time, so later mutations inside `./mod` do not update the local `count` variable.
archetypes.governingInvariant: module state updates propagate via live bindings or accessor functions while singleton initialization runs once

cognitiveTraps.name: Destructured CJS Primitive Stale Copy
cognitiveTraps.description: Destructuring a primitive property from `require()` captures a snapshot value that does not reflect subsequent updates in the source module.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const { count, inc } = require('./counter'); inc(); console.log(count); // still 0.

cognitiveTraps.name: Reassigning Imported ESM Live Binding
cognitiveTraps.description: Attempting to mutate or reassign an imported ESM binding in the consumer module throws `TypeError: Assignment to constant variable`.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: import { count } from './counter.js'; count += 1; // TypeError.

realWorldDomains.description: Tracing cross-module counter updates and singleton cache behavior in a telemetry pipeline.

qualityChecks.check: Shared module state is exposed through explicit getter/setter or factory functions rather than raw mutable `let` exports.
qualityChecks.why: Mutable `let` exports create hidden coupling and behave inconsistently between ESM live bindings and CJS value copies.

qualityChecks.check: Module-level registries or caches initialize idempotently so repeated calls do not duplicate entries.
qualityChecks.why: Non-idempotent initialization corrupts singleton state when multiple modules depend on the same service.

archetypes.name: Concurrent Promise.all & Async Composition
archetypes.coreConcept: Composing independent asynchronous tasks concurrently via `Promise.all` so total latency equals the slowest task while preserving input order in the output array.
mentalModel: 1. `await` pauses only the enclosing `async` function, not the JavaScript event loop.
2. Awaiting inside a `for...of` loop serializes independent tasks; mapping tasks to promises first and passing them to `Promise.all` starts all of them concurrently.
3. `Promise.all` resolves with results in the same order as the input iterable, regardless of completion order, and rejects fast on the first failure.
archetypes.governingInvariant: independent async tasks start concurrently and resolve in input order via Promise.all

cognitiveTraps.name: Sequential Await in Loop
cognitiveTraps.description: Awaiting each independent async call inside a loop forces serial execution, multiplying total latency by N.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: for (const id of ids) { results.push(await fetchItem(id)); } // takes N * latency instead of max(latency).

cognitiveTraps.name: Unawaited Async forEach Callback
cognitiveTraps.description: Using `items.forEach(async (item) => ...)` ignores the returned promises, so the enclosing function resolves before any async work finishes.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: items.forEach(async (x) => out.push(await work(x))); return out; // returns [].

realWorldDomains.description: Fetching independent user profile, permissions, and billing summaries concurrently for an API gateway.

qualityChecks.check: Independent async operations are started concurrently and awaited together rather than serialized inside a loop.
qualityChecks.why: Sequential `await` in a loop turns O(1) parallel I/O latency into O(N) total wait time.

qualityChecks.check: Async collection processing uses `Promise.all(items.map(...))` or `for...of` when ordering is required, never `Array.prototype.forEach` with an `async` callback.
qualityChecks.why: `forEach` discards returned promises, causing callers to observe incomplete state and unhandled rejections.

archetypes.name: Resilient Batch Aggregation with Promise.allSettled
archetypes.coreConcept: Using `Promise.allSettled` to await all concurrent tasks to completion and partition fulfilled outcomes from rejection reasons without losing successful work.
mentalModel: 1. `Promise.all` short-circuits on the first rejection, discarding other fulfilled results.
2. `Promise.allSettled` always resolves once every input promise settles, yielding `{ status: 'fulfilled', value }` or `{ status: 'rejected', reason }` in input order.
3. Callers must discriminate on `result.status` before reading `value` or `reason`.
archetypes.governingInvariant: every input task settles and is partitioned into fulfilled values or rejected reasons in input order

cognitiveTraps.name: Fail-Fast Promise.all on Partial Batch
cognitiveTraps.description: Using `Promise.all` when partial failures must be collected causes a single rejected task to abort the entire batch.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: await Promise.all(targets.map(ping)); // one timeout throws and hides all healthy targets.

cognitiveTraps.name: Detached Promise Rejection Before Await
cognitiveTraps.description: Creating a promise before awaiting an earlier throwing operation leaves the second promise unattached if it rejects first.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const p2 = stepTwo(); await stepOneThrows(); await p2; // p2 rejects unhandled.

realWorldDomains.description: Probing multiple service endpoints concurrently and reporting both healthy latencies and per-endpoint failures.

qualityChecks.check: `Promise.allSettled` results explicitly branch on `outcome.status === 'fulfilled'` vs `'rejected'` before accessing `value` or `reason`.
qualityChecks.why: Reading `.value` on a rejected outcome returns `undefined` and silently corrupts aggregated results.

qualityChecks.check: Rejected outcomes preserve the underlying error message or `Error` reason rather than swallowing it into a generic boolean or empty string.
qualityChecks.why: Discarding rejection reasons makes partial-batch failures impossible to diagnose in logs or API responses.

archetypes.name: Promise.race Timeout Guard & Timer Cleanup
archetypes.coreConcept: Racing an async operation against a bounded timeout with `Promise.race` while clearing the timer handle in `finally` and awaiting inside `try/catch` so rejections are caught and no timers leak.
mentalModel: 1. `Promise.race` settles with the first promise to fulfill or reject, but does NOT cancel the losing promises.
2. Any `setTimeout` created for a race deadline must be cleared in `finally` once the race settles.
3. Inside `async` functions, `try { return fn(); } catch` does NOT catch async rejections unless `return await fn()` is used.
archetypes.governingInvariant: race settles with the earliest outcome and always clears its deadline timer in finally

cognitiveTraps.name: Dangling Timeout Handle After Race
cognitiveTraps.description: Omitting `clearTimeout` in a `finally` block leaves the timeout timer pending after the main operation resolves.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Promise.race([work(), new Promise((_, rej) => setTimeout(() => rej(new Error('timeout')), ms))]); // timer leaks.

cognitiveTraps.name: Returning Unawaited Promise Inside try/catch
cognitiveTraps.description: Using `return asyncFn()` instead of `return await asyncFn()` inside `try` exits the `try` block before the promise settles, bypassing `catch`.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: async function safe() { try { return failingAsync(); } catch (e) { return null; } } // rejects instead of returning null.

realWorldDomains.description: Enforcing strict per-call SLA deadlines on RPC requests without leaking Node.js event-loop timers.

qualityChecks.check: Timeout guards paired with `Promise.race` always clear their timer handle in a `finally` block (or both settle paths) so fast completions do not leak active timers.
qualityChecks.why: Uncleaned `setTimeout` handles keep Node.js event loops and test runners open until the full timeout expires.

qualityChecks.check: Async calls whose rejections must be handled by a surrounding `try/catch` are `await`ed before returning.
qualityChecks.why: Returning a promise directly from `try` hands the unsettled promise to the caller and skips the `catch` block.

archetypes.name: Sync vs. Microtask vs. Macrotask Execution Order
archetypes.coreConcept: Predicting exact execution order across synchronous call-stack frames, synchronous `Promise` executor bodies, FIFO microtasks (`Promise.then`, `queueMicrotask`), and macrotasks (`setTimeout`).
mentalModel: 1. Synchronous top-level code and `new Promise(executor)` bodies run immediately on the Call Stack.
2. Once the Call Stack empties, the Event Loop drains the entire Microtask Queue in FIFO order (including microtasks enqueued by microtasks).
3. Only when the Microtask Queue is empty does the Event Loop dequeue one Macrotask (e.g. `setTimeout(..., 0)`), run it to completion, and drain microtasks again.
archetypes.governingInvariant: call stack empties -> all queued microtasks drain FIFO -> one macrotask runs -> repeat

cognitiveTraps.name: Macrotask Ordered Before Microtask
cognitiveTraps.description: Assuming `setTimeout(fn, 0)` runs immediately after synchronous code before queued `.then` or `queueMicrotask` callbacks.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: setTimeout(() => log('T'), 0); Promise.resolve().then(() => log('M')); // outputs M then T, not T then M.

cognitiveTraps.name: Assuming Promise Executor Runs Asynchronously
cognitiveTraps.description: Treating the callback passed to `new Promise((resolve) => { ... })` as a microtask instead of synchronous execution.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: new Promise((r) => { log('A'); r(); }); log('B'); // outputs A then B, not B then A.

realWorldDomains.description: Ordering synchronous event capture, microtask batching, and macrotask transport timers in a client telemetry SDK.

qualityChecks.check: Microtask callbacks (`Promise.then`, `queueMicrotask`) are drained completely in FIFO order after the synchronous call stack empties and before the next macrotask (`setTimeout`) begins.
qualityChecks.why: Misordering microtasks after `setTimeout(..., 0)` causes race conditions and wrong execution-order traces.

qualityChecks.check: Scheduling helpers avoid arbitrary positive timer delays when `0`-delay macrotasks or microtasks express the intended queue boundary.
qualityChecks.why: Magic delays like `setTimeout(fn, 25)` hide queue semantics and introduce flakiness under load.

archetypes.name: Async/Await Suspension & Microtask Continuation
archetypes.coreConcept: Tracing how `async` functions execute synchronously up to the first `await`, suspend and return a pending promise, and resume their post-`await` continuation as a microtask once the awaited value settles.
mentalModel: 1. Calling an `async` function runs its body synchronously until the first `await` expression is evaluated.
2. The `await` expression itself is evaluated synchronously; the remainder of the `async` function is scheduled as a microtask continuation.
3. Interleaved `.then()` chains and `await` continuations advance one microtask hop per turn in FIFO order.
archetypes.governingInvariant: pre-await runs synchronously; post-await resumes in the microtask queue after the awaited promise settles

cognitiveTraps.name: Assuming Entire Async Function Body Is Deferred
cognitiveTraps.description: Believing that calling `runTask()` where `runTask` is `async` defers statements written before the first `await`.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: async function f() { log('1'); await 0; log('2'); } f(); log('3'); // outputs 1, 3, 2.

cognitiveTraps.name: Misordering Chained Microtask Hops
cognitiveTraps.description: Evaluating an entire `.then().then()` chain or `await` sequence atomically instead of interleaving hop-by-hop with sibling microtasks.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Promise.resolve().then(() => log('a1')).then(() => log('a2')); Promise.resolve().then(() => log('b1')); // a1, b1, a2.

realWorldDomains.description: Tracing interleaved cache checks, async token refreshes, and queued request continuations.

qualityChecks.check: Code paths before the first `await` in an `async` function are treated as synchronous execution on the caller's stack, not deferred work.
qualityChecks.why: Assuming `async` defers the whole function body leads to wrong ordering of initialization side effects.

qualityChecks.check: Multi-step async traces preserve exact FIFO microtask-hop ordering across interleaved `await` resumptions and `.then()` callbacks.
qualityChecks.why: Each `.then` or `await` resumption enqueues only the next step after the previous step settles.

archetypes.name: Microtask Starvation & Cooperative Macrotask Yielding
archetypes.coreConcept: Diagnosing and fixing event-loop starvation where recursive `queueMicrotask` or `Promise.then` loops exhaustively drain the microtask queue and block pending macrotasks (`setTimeout`), by yielding between batches via macrotask scheduling.
mentalModel: 1. Because the Event Loop drains the entire Microtask Queue before taking the next Macrotask, self-enqueuing microtasks starve `setTimeout` and I/O.
2. `await Promise.resolve()` inside a loop yields only to sibling microtasks, NOT to macrotasks.
3. Yielding between chunks via a macrotask (`setTimeout(..., 0)`) lets already-queued timers and I/O run before the next batch.
archetypes.governingInvariant: yielding via a macrotask boundary allows queued timers and I/O to execute between work chunks

cognitiveTraps.name: Recursive Microtask Starving Macrotasks
cognitiveTraps.description: Scheduling the next work chunk with `queueMicrotask` or `Promise.resolve().then(...)` prevents any `setTimeout` macrotask from running until all chunks finish.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function step() { if (n-- > 0) queueMicrotask(step); } // blocks setTimeout(..., 0) until n reaches 0.

cognitiveTraps.name: Yielding With await Promise.resolve() Expecting Timer Progress
cognitiveTraps.description: Using `await Promise.resolve()` inside a batch loop still stays inside the microtask checkpoint and starves macrotasks.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: for (const c of chunks) { work(c); await Promise.resolve(); } // timer callback still runs only after loop completes.

realWorldDomains.description: Processing large in-memory log batches cooperatively so health-check timers and heartbeat callbacks still fire on time.

qualityChecks.check: Cooperative batch processors yield via a macrotask boundary (`setTimeout(..., 0)`) rather than `queueMicrotask` or `Promise.resolve().then(...)` so pending timers and I/O are not starved.
qualityChecks.why: Microtask checkpoints drain completely before the next macrotask, starving timers when work self-schedules as microtasks.

qualityChecks.check: Chunked schedulers advance work in bounded slices and avoid mutating caller-owned input arrays.
qualityChecks.why: Unbounded synchronous loops block the call stack and mutating caller arrays introduces hidden side effects.

archetypes.name: Typed Error Subclasses & Cause Chain Propagation
archetypes.coreConcept: Wrapping low-level failures in domain-specific `Error` subclasses using `super(message, { cause })` so callers can branch on error types (`instanceof` or `.code`) while preserving the original root cause.
mentalModel: 1. Always throw `Error` subclasses (setting `this.name` and structured metadata like `code` or `statusCode`), never raw strings or plain objects.
2. Pass `{ cause: err }` to `super(message, { cause })` whenever translating a lower-level error into a domain error.
3. Callers inspect `err instanceof DomainError` for recovery and walk `err.cause` for root-cause diagnostics.
archetypes.governingInvariant: translatedError instanceof Error && translatedError.cause === originalError

cognitiveTraps.name: Throwing New Domain Error Without Cause
cognitiveTraps.description: Constructing `new ServiceError(msg)` in a `catch` block without `{ cause: err }` discards the original error and stack trace.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: catch (err) { throw new ServiceError('Failed'); } // err.cause is undefined

cognitiveTraps.name: Throwing Raw Strings or Plain Objects
cognitiveTraps.description: Using `throw 'bad input'` or `throw { code: 'ERR' }` produces non-Error values without stack traces or `instanceof Error`.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: throw 'CONFIG_MISSING'; // err instanceof Error === false, err.stack === undefined

realWorldDomains.description: Translating low-level transport/JSON errors into typed PaymentGatewayError instances with preserved cause chains.

qualityChecks.check: When catching and re-throwing a lower-level error as a domain error, the original error is attached via `{ cause: err }`.
qualityChecks.why: Omitting `{ cause }` destroys the underlying stack trace and root-cause context needed for debugging.

qualityChecks.check: Custom errors extend `Error` (passing `message` and `{ cause }` to `super`) and are thrown as `Error` instances, never raw strings or plain objects.
qualityChecks.why: Raw strings and plain objects lack stack traces and break `instanceof Error` checks at catch boundaries.

archetypes.name: Async Boundary Error Propagation & Cleanup
archetypes.coreConcept: Ensuring `async`/`await` boundaries propagate failures cleanly instead of swallowing exceptions in `catch`, while releasing resources in `finally` without overriding active return values or thrown errors.
mentalModel: 1. An empty `catch` or silent fallback (`return null` / `return {}`) turns a loud failure into silent data corruption.
2. `finally` runs on both normal completion and throw, so it is for cleanup only.
3. Never `return` or throw blindly inside `finally` because it suppresses the `try`/`catch` outcome.
archetypes.governingInvariant: cleanup runs in finally && unhandled operational errors propagate to caller

cognitiveTraps.name: Swallowing Errors With Silent Fallback
cognitiveTraps.description: Catching an exception and returning a default value (`null`, `[]`, `{}`) masks failures and corrupts downstream callers.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: try { return await fetchUser(id); } catch (e) { return null; } // network outage looks like missing user

cognitiveTraps.name: Returning Inside Finally Block
cognitiveTraps.description: A `return` statement inside `finally` silently discards any exception thrown in `try` or `catch`.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: try { throw new Error('boom'); } finally { return 'ok'; } // returns 'ok', error vanishes

realWorldDomains.description: Acquiring and releasing a lock around async work while propagating operational errors intact.

qualityChecks.check: Error handlers never silently swallow unexpected errors by returning dummy fallbacks; they either recover a specific expected case or propagate the error.
qualityChecks.why: Silent fallbacks hide root causes and turn failed operations into misleading empty results.

qualityChecks.check: `finally` blocks perform cleanup only and never `return` a value that overrides `try` or `catch` outcomes.
qualityChecks.why: Returning from `finally` suppresses thrown errors and replaces the intended return value.

archetypes.name: Operational vs. Programmer Error Boundary Refactor
archetypes.coreConcept: Distinguishing expected operational errors (mapped to structured domain responses or typed errors) from programmer bugs (`TypeError`, `RangeError`, invariant violations that must re-throw), and flattening nested `try/catch` blocks into focused boundary helpers.
mentalModel: 1. Operational errors (invalid user input, missing record, upstream timeout) are expected and handled/mapped at the boundary.
2. Programmer bugs (`TypeError` from `null.prop`, `ReferenceError`) must never be caught and disguised as `404` or `{ ok: false, reason: 'not_found' }`.
3. Extract small boundary helpers so validation, execution, and error translation stay flat and single-purpose.
archetypes.governingInvariant: operational errors map to typed boundary outcomes; programmer errors re-throw

cognitiveTraps.name: Blanket Catch Masking Programmer Bugs
cognitiveTraps.description: A blanket `catch (err)` maps all errors—including `TypeError` or `RangeError`—into a generic operational error response.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: catch (err) { return { ok: false, code: 'NOT_FOUND' }; } // masks TypeError inside business logic

cognitiveTraps.name: Deeply Nested Try/Catch Control Flow
cognitiveTraps.description: Nesting `try/catch` blocks inside business logic mixes error translation with domain steps and drops context.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: try { try { ... } catch (e1) { ... } } catch (e2) { ... }

realWorldDomains.description: Refactoring a tangled webhook handler into clean validation, signature verification, and typed error boundaries.

qualityChecks.check: Catch blocks check for specific expected operational errors and re-throw unexpected programmer errors (`TypeError`, `RangeError`, unknown errors).
qualityChecks.why: Converting programmer bugs into operational error responses hides defects and makes debugging impossible.

qualityChecks.check: Boundary functions use one consistent error contract (either structured Result `{ ok, value | error }` or throwing typed `Error` subclasses), never mixing `null` returns and throws ambiguously.
qualityChecks.why: Mixing `null` returns with exceptions forces callers to check both channels and causes missed error paths.
